limits: No individual employee adverse-action chain is completely recovered.
The final public amount is EUR 15 million, not EUR 32 million.
cases.title: Amazon France Logistique scanner telemetry and performance monitoring
cases.transaction_summary: Scanner-linked warehouse activity and performance indicators were processed at individual granularity; the CNIL imposed an initial EUR 32 million sanction and the Conseil d’État later partially reformed the decision and reduced the fine to EUR 15 million.

limits: The release records agency findings and citation, not every contested fact or worker-level outcome.
cases.title: Amazon California undisclosed peer-to-peer warehouse quotas
cases.transaction_summary: California cited Amazon for failing to give written quota and discipline notice at Moreno Valley and Redlands warehouses; the employer described the system as peer-to-peer evaluation while the regulator applied the statute’s functional quota definition.

limits: Separate enforcement records are not summed into one liability figure.
No individual rider’s complete assignment-to-exclusion chain is reconstructed.

cases.title: Foodinho / Glovo repeated rider algorithm enforcement
cases.transaction_summary: Foodinho rider-management systems joined geolocation, order acceptance, delivery history, feedback and device data to rating and work-opportunity allocation; Italian enforcement records imposed sanctions in 2021 and 2024 and required contestability and corrective measures.

limits: The company stated the shift-booking system was no longer used by the end of 2020.
No current deployment is inferred from the 2021 record.

cases.title: Deliveroo Italy geolocation, assignment and human-intervention enforcement
cases.transaction_summary: Italian enforcement records addressed opaque order-assignment and shift-booking algorithms, frequent geolocation, extensive rider data and the need for substantive human intervention and periodic checks for distorted or discriminatory effects.

cases.jurisdiction: Netherlands / United Kingdom-facing platform decisions / European Union data law
limits: The public court release does not itself establish every underlying fraud allegation or every later remedy.
cases.title: Uber and Ola automated fraud scores and account removal explanations
cases.transaction_summary: The Amsterdam Court of Appeal treated trip allocation, pricing, internal scores and fraud-related account removal as fully automated significant decisions and required Uber and Ola to provide factors, reasons and information necessary to understand and contest them.

limits: Through 2027-05-31 OLS enforcement is limited to procedure and cannot determine whether the deactivation reason was permissible.
The records describe allegations and informal resolutions.
cases.title: Seattle app-worker deactivation procedure enforcement
cases.transaction_summary: Seattle’s 2025 public records show procedure-focused enforcement producing restarted deactivation processes, reinstatement or reactivation and worker payments for Amazon Flex, DoorDash, Gopuff and Grubhub matters.
